title: Intelligence
subtitle: What your own posts measured, explained in plain language, with drafts you control. Nothing posts automatically.

labelHints.measured: Numbers reported by the platforms for your posts. Blank means the platform did not report it.
labelHints.calculated: Statistics computed from your measured numbers. No guessing, no industry averages.
labelHints.predicted: An estimate with a confidence level. Treat as a hint, not a fact.
labelHints.recommended: A suggestion built from your measured evidence. You decide whether to act on it.
labelHints.declared: Information you entered about this brand. Intelligence compares results against it.
labelHints.generated: Text written by AI from your own evidence and brand voice. Always saved as a draft you can edit.

page.title: How Intelligence works
page.intro: Intelligence reads the posts you have already published, keeps every number exactly as the platforms reported it, and turns that history into plain-language answers: what worked, when to post, what to try next. You stay in control of every action.
steps: Pick a brand. Everything on this page is scoped to one brand and its connected channels.
Start on Overview to see what has been measured so far and which features have enough data to switch on.
Set your objective and audience under Audience. It decides which metric every recommendation optimizes for.
Read Content, Opportunities, and Playbook for evidence-backed answers, then use Draft this to turn any of them into a post draft.
Every draft lands in Content as a normal draft. Review, edit, schedule, or delete it like any other post.
inputs: Posts published through Markaestro and posts imported from your connected accounts
The metrics each platform reports for those posts (views, reach, likes, comments, shares, saves, clicks)
Your declared objective, markets, timezone, pillars, and brand voice
never: Publish or schedule anything on its own
Fill in a number a platform did not report
Use other brands' data or generic industry benchmarks

overview.title: Overview
overview.intro: A snapshot of what has been measured for this brand, plus a readiness list that tells you exactly which features are active and what is still missing.
steps: Check the objective banner. Every ranking and recommendation uses that metric.
Read the KPI tiles. A blank tile means no connected platform reported that metric, never zero.
Use the readiness list to see how close each feature is to switching on and what to do about it.
Compare platforms per post, not by total, so a channel with fewer posts is judged fairly.
inputs: All synced posts for this brand and their latest reported metrics
Your objective from the Audience tab
never: Mix numbers from different brands
Estimate metrics a platform left blank

audience.title: Audience
audience.intro: Tell Intelligence who you create for and what success means. This profile is the yardstick for Audience Fit in the composer, for timing, and for every recommendation.
steps: Choose an objective. It picks the metric Intelligence optimizes for (for example Engagement uses likes, comments, shares, and saves).
Add your primary market, timezone, content pillars, and voice traits. Posting windows are calculated in this timezone.
Create tracked links for the URLs you share. Each click is counted here without storing personal data.
Save. Changes apply on the next refresh.
inputs: What you enter on this tab
Clicks on your tracked links and conversions you send to Markaestro
never: Store IP addresses, browser details, or referrers from tracked links
Change your profile automatically

content.title: Content
content.intro: Your measured posts ranked by the metric you chose, with the patterns Intelligence recognized in each one and a plain-language explanation of why it performed the way it did.
steps: Sort by your objective, views, or engagements. Filter to one platform to compare like with like.
Open Why it worked on any post for a short explanation grounded in that post's numbers versus your account average.
Use Draft a post like this to get a new caption that reuses what worked, saved to Content as a draft.
Check the lowest measured posts too: what is missing there is often the clearest lesson.
inputs: Each post's caption, platform, publish time, and reported metrics
Content patterns (pillar, hook, format) detected from the caption of each published post
never: Rank posts on metrics that were not reported
Edit or repost anything without you

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.intro: Concrete things to try next, each backed by your own numbers: a posting window that outperforms your average, a platform that does better per post, or a pattern worth repeating.
steps: Read the evidence line under each card. It shows the exact numbers behind the suggestion.
Accept if you plan to try it, Pin to revisit, or Dismiss if it does not fit. All three can be undone.
Use Draft this to get a caption written for that opportunity, saved to Content as a draft.
Publish from Content or Calendar as usual. Accepting never creates or schedules posts.
inputs: Best posting windows, per-post platform comparison, and playbook learnings
Your objective and platform priority from the Audience tab
never: Suggest something with fewer than five measured posts behind it
Act on an accepted opportunity without you

playbook.title: Playbook
playbook.intro: Patterns that repeat in your data with enough posts to matter: which platform, hook, pillar, format, or time slot performs above or below the rest of this brand.
steps: Each card compares a group of posts against every other post of this brand on your objective metric.
The effect is the percent difference per post. The 95% range tells you how sure the estimate is.
Strength grows with sample size: directional (5 to 14 posts), moderate (15 to 29), potentially strong (30 or more with a clear range).
Accept patterns you want to repeat, then use Draft this to write a post in that pattern.
inputs: Measured posts grouped by platform, pillar, hook, format, and weekday/hour
Content patterns detected from each published caption
never: Report a pattern with fewer than five posts in the group and five outside it
Claim a cause. These are associations in your own data.

advanced.title: Experiments and Ask Markaestro
advanced.intro: Test one idea at a time with a paired A/B post, and ask questions that are answered only from this brand's measured records.
steps: Create an experiment: one platform, two variants, one window. Both posts are scheduled for you.
When the window ends, the winner is decided by the measured metric and lands in your Inbox.
Ask Markaestro picks one approved data tool per question and cites the records it used.
Campaigns are a preview: you can name them now, post assignment is coming.
inputs: Both experiment posts and their reported metrics
Stored learnings, comparisons, timing, and top posts for Ask Markaestro
never: Declare a winner without the measured difference and sample behind it
Answer from generic social-media advice

drafts.title: Draft this
drafts.intro: Turns an opportunity, a pattern, or a specific post into a new caption written in your brand voice from your own best-performing evidence.
steps: Intelligence gathers up to five of your strongest measured posts for that opportunity or pattern, plus your audience profile and brand voice.
The draft is written for the chosen platform, with hashtags and a hook, and a short note on which evidence shaped it.
It is saved as a draft in Content. Open it, edit it, add media, and schedule it when you are ready.
inputs: Your measured posts, the audience profile, and the brand voice you declared
The evidence behind the opportunity or pattern you clicked
never: Publish or schedule the draft
Invent claims, prices, offers, or links that are not in your brand data

explain.title: Why it worked
explain.intro: A short explanation of one post's result compared with the rest of your account: what stood out in the caption, the timing, or the platform average.
steps: Open it on any measured post. The explanation is generated once and stored with the post.
Factors point at real things: a metric, the caption, a detected pattern, or the timing window.
Use the Try next suggestion as a hypothesis for your next post or an experiment.
inputs: That post's numbers, caption, and detected patterns
Your platform averages and best posting window
never: Claim a cause. It describes associations in your data.
Use metrics the platform did not report

links.title: Tracked links
links.intro: Short links you paste into captions so clicks can be counted and, with the conversion API, tied back to sales or sign-ups.
steps: Create a link with a label and destination. Copy the short URL into any caption.
Clicks appear here as they happen. No IP address, browser, or referrer is stored.
Send conversion events to the API with the click id to see attributed conversions per link.
inputs: Redirects through the short link
Conversion events your site or server sends to Markaestro
never: Track visitors across sites
Store personal data from a click
